deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84): Grothendieck studies an arrangement Σ of n pseudo-lines indexed by I in the projective plane. Ĩ is the doubled index set, with 2n elements: each line with its two orientations, or equivalently its two 'ends', related by an antipodism. For an auxiliary pseudo-line D in Σ's 'space of positions', the trace of Σ on D (more precisely on a double cover of D) gives a cyclic polygon Pol(D) whose vertices are labelled by Ĩ, compatible with the antipodism. In modern terms this is the local or circular sequence of D, i.e. an allowable sequence in the sense of Goodman–Pollack.

The previous page sets up the following. The vertices of a graph Γ(Σ) are 'critical' positions of D. For these he builds the polygons P(Δ) and P̂(Δ) of order 2(n−1), and a canonical map from vertices of Γ(Σ) to antipodism-compatible polygonal structures on Ĩ. He claims this map is injective. He then sets two tasks: (1) follow P and P̂ along a specialization arrow D→D'; (2) recover the whole oriented-graph structure (alternating polygons, orientation of edges and corners) from the polygonal-structure interpretation.

This page treats task (1) in the 'ordinary' case, where D' is a specialization of D. The figures show the green line D pushed across a crossing of two orange pseudo-lines, so that D' passes through or beyond that crossing.
- Local comparison: the coverings (cartes) Pol(D) and Pol(D') of D̃̃ and D̃̃' coincide everywhere except near the two antipodal segments attached to the specialization edge a and its antipode. At D' the situation is the reverse.
- First precise statement: there is a canonical isomorphism P̂(D) ≅ P̂(D'). It sends a vertex σ of P̂(D) coming from ā to the antipodal vertex σ' of P̂(D') coming from ā.
- Second formulation: let a' be the 'opposite' specialization edge on D'. Deleting vertex a from Pol(D) and vertex a' from Pol(D') gives isomorphic polygons, with a sent to a'. Equivalently, there is a unique edge γ of D such that the derived polygon Pol'(D), with a new vertex a'' inserted, is isomorphic to Pol(D'), extending the previous isomorphism.
- Orientations: the isomorphism is compatible with orientations. Corresponding edges, as modified edges of P(Σ), carry equal orientations, and so do the corner orientations (angles α, β versus α', β' in the figure).

Combinatorially, this is the statement that crossing a vertex changes the circular sequence only by a local move: an adjacent transposition, together with its antipodal copy. The page breaks off mid-sentence, and task (2) is not addressed here.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The page is heuristic and incomplete: the 'ordinary' case is the only one treated, and the orientation-compatibility statement is cut off mid-sentence.

The two formulations, (isomorphism P̂(D)≅P̂(D') with σ mapped to the antipodal σ') and (deleting a and a'), are asserted from the picture rather than proved. The injectivity of the vertex → polygonal-structure map, from the previous page, also remains unproved.

ideas.what: Associating to a position of an extra pseudo-line D the cyclic, antipodally symmetric sequence of crossings with Σ (a polygon on Ĩ)
ideas.modern_name: Local/circular sequences; allowable sequences; single-element extensions of rank-3 oriented matroids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, ~1980-84); Las Vergnas, Bland (oriented matroid extensions, late 1970s)
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Montpellier notes; pseudo-lines are not treated in Esquisse or R&S as far as I know

ideas.what: Comparison of the polygons for D and its specialization D' (a pseudo-line pushed across a crossing): they agree except near two antipodal segments; isomorphism after deleting/inserting one vertex, compatible with orientations
ideas.modern_name: Local move (adjacent transposition) of allowable sequences under a mutation/triangle flip; edges of the extension space graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956) for flips; Goodman–Pollack for allowable sequences; Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993) for extension spaces

ideas.what: Programme to reconstruct the full oriented graph Γ(Σ) (alternating polygons, oriented edges and corners) from its vertices viewed as polygonal structures on Ĩ
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial description of the extension space / flip graph of a pseudoline arrangement

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes to characterise the entire oriented graph of critical positions of an added pseudo-line purely from the antipodal polygonal structures on Ĩ. This would give an intrinsic combinatorial model of the 'space of pseudo-lines relative to Σ' including orientation data on edges and corners. The task is posed but left undone on this page.
missed.quote: Comment interpréter toute la structure de graphe orienté : polygones alternés, avec orientations des arêtes et des coins, en termes de l'interprétation de ses sommets comme des str. polygonales sur Ĩ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is close to describing extension spaces of rank-3 oriented matroids, which are known to be subtle (Sturmfels–Ziegler, Mnëv–Ziegler). The specific orientation data on 'alternating polygons' may be a distinctive encoding, but it largely overlaps the known theory.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine local computation in a little-known Grothendieck project: how circular sequences change when a pseudo-line crosses a vertex. It is essentially the known allowable-sequence or flip calculus. The broader programme is historically interesting, but this page adds no new result.
